# Incident Report: Malware Infection — DESKTOP-ES9F3ML (2026-01-31)

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.1.21.58** |
| MAC address | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** (Intel NIC) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** |
| AD domain | WIN11OFFICE.COM (NetBIOS: WIN11OFFICE) |
| Logged-in user | **gwyatt** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString exchanges with the domain controller 10.1.21.2) |

Only one host on the /24 (besides the gateway 10.1.21.1 and domain controller 10.1.21.2) generated traffic in this capture, so `gwyatt`'s workstation is the sole affected asset visible in this evidence.

## 2. Malware Family

**SecTopRAT (aka ArechClient2)** — attribution is **behavioral, not signature-confirmed** (no IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence directory; conclusion is based solely on traffic-pattern analysis of the pcap).

Basis for the behavioral call:
- Infection vector matches SecTopRAT's known SEO-poisoning / fake-download-portal delivery: the host browsed a chain of cloned/lookalike download domains (`hiyter.com`, `media.megafilehub4.lat`, `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`, all Cloudflare-fronted) immediately before a 16 MB TLS download from `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (104.21.46.67:443, frame 2776, 22 seconds) — consistent with a bundled/inflated loader installer.
- ~42 seconds after that download, the host began communicating with `whitepepper.su` (153.92.1.49) using an HTTP(S) API path unique to this family: `GET /api/set_agent?id=<bot_id>&token=<token>&description=&agent=<Browser>`, which returns an HTML/JS payload that fingerprints the browser (WebGL, canvas, WebRTC, AudioContext, plugins, navigator properties) and POSTs the results back to the same endpoint with `&act=log`. This exact `set_agent`/`id`/`token`/`act=log` browser-fingerprint harvesting pattern is a signature TTP of SecTopRAT, which drives a real installed browser (Chrome/Edge, confirmed by matching JA3 hashes shared with legitimate same-session Adobe traffic) rather than shipping its own TLS stack.
- Sustained low-and-slow beaconing to the same C2 (`whitepepper.su`) followed: roughly 20+ short-lived TCP/TLS sessions on ports 80 and 443 between t+92s and t+122s, a cadence consistent with C2 polling/tasking rather than normal web browsing.
- Two follow-on connections to sibling infrastructure (`holiday-forever.cc` and `communicationfirewall-security.cc`) immediately after, pulling ~100+ KB each — consistent with secondary config/module retrieval.

No executable payload was recoverable from the capture itself (the loader and any post-infection modules were transferred over TLS), so no binary hash can be produced for the malware itself. Hashes below are for the plaintext artifacts actually captured.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

### Command-and-control endpoints (IP:port)
| IP:port | Domain (SNI/Host) | Role |
|---|---|---|
| 153.92.1.49:443, 153.92.1.49:80 | whitepepper.su | Primary C2 — fingerprint-collection gate + persistent beaconing |
| 62.72.32.156:443 | whooptm.cyou | Gate/redirector immediately preceding whitepepper.su |
| 80.97.160.24:443 | holiday-forever.cc | Secondary C2/module retrieval |
| 104.21.9.36:443 | communicationfirewall-security.cc | Secondary C2/module retrieval (Cloudflare-fronted) |
| 104.21.46.67:443 | arch.filemegahab4.sbs | Payload delivery (16 MB download, Cloudflare-fronted) |

### Malicious domains
- `whitepepper.su`
- `whooptm.cyou`
- `holiday-forever.cc`
- `communicationfirewall-security.cc`
- `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`
- `media.megafilehub4.lat`
- `hiyter.com`

### Malicious URLs
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log` (POST, fingerprint exfil)
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log` (POST, fingerprint exfil)

Bot ID observed: `3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C`
C2 token observed: `842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b`

### Transferred files / SHA256 (plaintext artifacts recovered from the capture)
| File | SHA256 | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| set_agent (Chrome, GET response) | `a1ee2e3055dc4ce0d60eb6c2c8a655e705b3607bd33d65794e67adf22a2a0124` | Fingerprint-harvesting HTML/JS served by C2 |
| set_agent&act=log (Chrome, POST body) | `713757395cb4bdc2f6786551ee10a32d465b53315fed9a4a1e03b8053506daf0` | Exfiltrated browser fingerprint |
| set_agent (Edge, GET response) | `8f97a4018d4b0675b9592660394cf5b73f1be2252e27aff64a8f160af9079f46` | Same harvesting page, second bot check-in |
| set_agent&act=log (Edge, POST body) | `2049fb3664b6b96eb36623732dfc5a01de8bc1f73e1adf5be6645b872cfd5063` | Exfiltrated browser fingerprint |
| favicon.ico (whitepepper.su) | `74ab801591b951bcb6b248a8ef9321388a45ecf8badd2893aea4aa360b26ea90` | Served by C2 infrastructure |

The actual loader/RAT binary was never observed in plaintext — it was delivered over TLS from `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (104.21.46.67), so no hash could be extracted from this pcap for it.

## 4. Recommended action
Isolate DESKTOP-ES9F3ML (10.1.21.58) from the network, reset `gwyatt`'s domain credentials, block the domains/IPs above at the perimeter, and forensically image the host to recover and hash the actual RAT binary for definitive signature confirmation.
